senses.gloss: to be rough, grating, scraping; v. גֵּרָה, גָּרוֹן &c.

units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 107b">Snh. 107ᵇ</cite> <he>שגי׳ דובים וכ׳</he> because he let the bears loose against the children.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 21:5">Ex. R. s. 21</cite> <he>ג׳ לפרעה</he> He incited Pharaoh &c.
Gen. R. s. 19, end (interpret. hishshiani, Gen. III, 13) גִּירַנִי.
Cant. R. to I, 4 (play on משכני ib.) ממה שגֵּרִיתָ בי שכני הרעים from my hostile neighbors whom thou hast incited against me.—Trnsf. ג׳ את הדוב ב־ to let temptation loose against.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 87">Gen. R. s. 87</cite> <he>אני מְגָרֶה בך וכ׳</he> I shall lay temptation in thy way; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 17:2">Lev. R. s. 17</cite> <he>ביום שיְגָרֶה וכ׳</he> on the day when the Lord shall stir up his anger &c.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 19a:10">Snh. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>מִתְגָּרוֹת זו בזו</he> jealous of one another.

<cite ref="Berakhot 7b:10">Ber. 7ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Megillah 6b:6">Meg. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>מותר להִתְגָּרוֹת וכ׳</he> it is permitted to enter into combat with the wicked (with reference to b. h. <he>התחרה</he>).—
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 19:22">Num. R. s. 19</cite> <he>נתג׳ בהם</he> he attacked them.

senses.gloss: to be let loose. Esth. R. introd. נִתְגָּרְתָה אותה הדוב that temptation was aroused (against Joseph), v. supra; Num. R. s. 13 מִתְגָּרַת.
to have a passion for, to indulge freely in.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 76b">Yoma 76ᵇ</cite> wine is called <he>תיר̇ש̇</he>, because he <he>המִתְגָּרֶה בו נעשה ר̇ש̇</he> who indulges in it becomes poor.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 18b">Ab. Zar. 18ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 19b:10">19ᵇ</cite> <he>אֶתְגָּרֶה בשינה</he> I will freely indulge in sleep (idleness).
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 18">Num. R. s. 18</cite>; Tanḥ. Koraḥ 3 <he>להִתְגָּרוֹת בו את וכֹ׳</he> to incite Israel against him.
